item.title: Star Blizzard RedFlick Campaigns and AI-Accelerated Exploitation Drive Security Alerts
item.content:encoded:
Window: 30 Sep 18:00 → 30 Sep 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

DIVD says Zammad zero-days enabled AI-driven network breach — Must Read

DIVD says attackers used two zero-day flaws in the Zammad helpdesk platform to hijack sessions, execute code, and gain root access in an AI-agent-driven breach. Zammad users are urged to upgrade to version 7 or take vulnerable instances offline.

  • DIVD says its network breach involved a chain of two zero-day vulnerabilities in the open-source Zammad ticketing system, identified as CVE-2026-102489 and CVE-2026-102490.
  • According to DIVD, the flaws could be combined to hijack sessions, run code remotely, and raise access from a Zammad user account to full server control.
  • DIVD said an autonomous AI agent carried out the actions in seconds and left explanations that helped investigators reconstruct the incident.
  • Network separation and DIVD's response actions prevented the attacker from moving deeper into the network, although the investigation remains ongoing.
  • DIVD recommends that Zammad users upgrade to version 7 or take affected instances offline as soon as possible.

Products: zammad

Vendors: zammad

Russian state hackers use new RedFlick technique to push malware — Should Read

Russian state-linked group Star Blizzard is using a new RedFlick phishing chain that requires victims only to open a disguised shortcut, then automatically installs the CosmicPulse backdoor through scheduled tasks and remotely hosted payloads. Microsoft says the campaigns have targeted Ukraine-related organizations, NGOs, governments, and financial institutions, primarily in the US and UK.

  • Microsoft reports that the Russian state actor Star Blizzard has begun using a malware-delivery method dubbed RedFlick to deploy its CosmicPulse backdoor.
  • RedFlick begins with phishing emails and a password-protected archive containing a virtual disk and a shortcut disguised as a PDF; opening the shortcut launches hidden commands while displaying a decoy document.
  • The infection chain installs scheduled tasks that collect computer and user information, enable access to remote web resources, and run remotely hosted follow-on code.
  • A downloader called NOROBOT and BAITSWITCH retrieves Python components and a bootstrapper that decrypts and launches CosmicPulse, which can execute attacker-supplied Python code, download and run files, or retrieve documents.
  • Microsoft observed at least 13 large-scale phishing campaigns since the start of the year, affecting more than 100 organizations, including Ukrainian targets and Ukraine-supporting NGOs, think tanks, governments, and financial institutions.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: windows, python-3-8

Vendors: microsoft, google, python

How Device Code Phishing Bypasses MFA in Microsoft 365 — Should Read

A live Microsoft 365 phishing campaign abuses the legitimate device code authentication flow to obtain valid, MFA-approved tokens without stealing passwords, then may deploy ConnectWise ScreenConnect for remote access. Organizations should restrict device code flow in Entra Conditional Access, investigate device-code sign-ins, and revoke active sessions/tokens after suspected compromise.

  • The phishing campaign abuses Microsoft’s legitimate device code sign-in process, allowing victims to complete normal Microsoft authentication and multi-factor authentication while authorizing a session on an attacker-controlled device.
  • A compromised Microsoft 365 identity can provide access to Exchange Online mail and calendars, OneDrive and SharePoint files, Teams conversations, and Entra ID directory information, depending on the user’s permissions.
  • The campaign’s second-stage page impersonates Adobe Acrobat and prompts victims to download an update that installs a vendor-signed ConnectWise ScreenConnect remote-support client configured for attacker access.
  • Traditional controls may not detect this technique because the sign-in occurs on a real Microsoft page, contains no password-capture form, satisfies MFA legitimately, and generates no endpoint activity during the identity compromise.
  • The article recommends restricting device code flow through Entra Conditional Access, hunting for device-code sign-ins, explicitly revoking sessions and tokens after suspected compromise, and reviewing delegated permissions and data access.

Technologies: cloud-platform, identity-provider, iam, mfa, remote-access

Products: microsoft-365, microsoft-entra-id, microsoft-graph, connectwise-screenconnect, cloudflare-turnstile

Vendors: microsoft, connectwise, cloudflare

Automakers routinely share personally identifiable connected-car data with third parties, report says — Should Read

A Consumer Reports and Northeastern University study found that 19 of 21 automakers and 28 of 30 connected-car apps share customer data with third parties, including advertisers, analytics firms, and major tech companies. Some apps transmitted personally identifiable information such as names, emails, precise locations, and VIN-linked data, potentially enabling tracking of drivers’ movements.

  • Northeastern University researchers and Consumer Reports found that 19 of 21 major automakers studied collect and broadly disseminate customer data from connected vehicles.
  • Twenty-eight of 30 connected-car apps examined shared data with at least one third-party advertising or analytics firm.
  • Seven of the 30 apps sent personally identifiable information, including names, email addresses, or precise locations, to at least one outside company.
  • Consumer Reports said GM’s myCadillac, myChevrolet, myBuick, and myGMC apps, along with Honda, Nissan, and Lincoln apps, shared VINs paired with location data or email addresses.
  • After Consumer Reports notified Honda of the findings, Honda directed a digital data analytics and tracking vendor to delete ingested location data and stop sharing it with third parties.

Technologies: iot-device

Products: mycadillac, mychevrolet, mybuick, mygmc

Vendors: general-motors, honda, nissan, lincoln, alphabet, amazon, microsoft, meta, reddit, pinterest

Over 543,000 valid credentials exposed in public GitHub repositories — Should Read

Truffle Security found 543,699 still-valid credentials publicly exposed across GitHub repositories, with a median exposure period of 784 days. GitHub Push Protection has reduced leaks for credential types it covers, but many exposed secrets remain unblocked or unrevoked, underscoring the need for rapid credential rotation.

  • Truffle Security identified 543,699 unique credentials that were still valid and publicly exposed in GitHub repositories, appearing across more than 1.1 million files and repositories including forks.
  • The analysis drew on a dataset covering 224 million repositories and more than 58 billion files, with a crawl that ended on August 7, 2025.
  • The median time a unique credential remained publicly accessible was 784 days, and about 10% of working credentials were more than 6.3 years old.
  • GitHub Push Protection reduced exposure of credential categories it covers by 53% after it was enabled by default, but 51.8% of live credentials belonged to categories it does not block by default.
  • Of 126,963 exposed Google Cloud service account credentials, 69,041 remained valid, while only one of 101,886 committed npm tokens still worked.

Technologies: source-control, ci-cd, cloud-platform, package-registry

Products: github-push-protection, google-cloud-service-accounts, npm

Vendors: github, truffle-security, google, npm, hugging-face

After reports on suicide deaths, Pentagon puts Cyber Command on notice — May Read

Following reports of suicide deaths among personnel, the Pentagon ordered U.S. Cyber Command to rapidly implement mental-health, workload recovery, and force-resiliency measures for its continuously deployed cyber operators.

  • Pentagon cyber policy official Katherine Sutton directed U.S. Cyber Command to implement mandatory wellness and resiliency measures after reports of suicide deaths within the command.
  • Cyber Command was ordered within 30 days to provide four years of organizational climate survey data and exit-interview summaries and to finalize an agreement with the National Security Agency to share mental and behavioral health professionals.
  • The command must establish a Cyber Occupational Resiliency and Engagement Framework and introduce workload phasing measures intended to make recovery time more predictable and reduce cumulative strain on Cyber Mission Force personnel.
  • Within 60 days, Cyber Command must submit a proposal to change consecutive-tour policies by adding career, instructor, and education assignments that interrupt continuous operational stress.
  • Senior military cyber officials said persistent high-tempo operations have made it necessary to develop rest plans and allow personnel to step away from continuous work against adversaries.

Google: Vulnerability disclosures double to 10,000 per month as AI fuels exploitation — Optional

Google says vulnerability disclosures rose from about 5,000 in January to 10,740 in August, while attackers are increasingly using AI to rapidly weaponize high-risk publicly disclosed flaws. Exploited vulnerabilities already exceed last year’s total, with perimeter appliances and exposed enterprise services remaining key targets.

  • Google’s Threat Intelligence Group reported that monthly vulnerability disclosures rose from 5,045 in January to 10,740 in August, exceeding 10,000 in both July and August.
  • The report said 141 vulnerabilities had been exploited in 2026 by the end of the eight-month period, compared with 127 during all of 2025.
  • Google assessed that the rise in exploitation is driven by rapid, targeted weaponization of high-risk publicly disclosed and patched flaws rather than a flood of newly discovered unknown flaws.
  • GTIG observed one threat cluster exploiting CVE-2026-1731 within four days of its public disclosure and five more clusters within seven days.
  • Fourteen percent of vulnerabilities exploited between January and August affected edge and security appliances, reflecting continued attacker focus on perimeter devices and exposed enterprise services.

Technologies: router

Vendors: google, beyondtrust, hacktron-ai, totolink, oracle

item.title: Active Cisco SD-WAN and Zimbra Exploitation Drives Critical Infrastructure Risk
item.content:encoded:
Window: 30 Sep 14:00 → 30 Sep 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

Cisco warns of new SD-WAN zero-day exploited in attacks — Must Read

Cisco is urging customers to immediately patch Catalyst SD-WAN Manager for CVE-2026-76504, a critical authentication-bypass zero-day actively exploited to grant remote, unauthenticated attackers administrator access.

  • Cisco released fixes for CVE-2026-76504, a critical Catalyst SD-WAN Manager flaw that the company says is being actively exploited.
  • The flaw lets an unauthenticated remote attacker gain administrator privileges by sending a crafted HTTP request that bypasses an authentication rule through improper URI encoding.
  • Cisco said all Catalyst SD-WAN Manager deployments are affected regardless of configuration and recommends upgrading to a fixed software release.
  • Cisco advised administrators to investigate serviceproxy-access.log and vmanage-server.log for j_security_check entries from unknown or unauthorized IP addresses, including requests using %6a for the letter "j".
  • CVE-2026-76504 is the fifth Cisco SD-WAN zero-day reported as actively exploited in 2026.

Technologies: network-monitoring, router

Products: catalyst-sd-wan-manager, sd-wan-vmanage, catalyst-sd-wan-controller

Vendors: cisco

Attackers Exploit Zimbra Flaw to Deploy Web Shells and Harvest Authentication Secrets — Must Read

Attackers are actively exploiting the patched Zimbra CVE-2026-73570 command-injection flaw to install web shells, steal mailbox and authentication data, and establish persistent remote access on exposed servers. Organizations should urgently update to Zimbra 10.1.20 or mitigate by removing zimbra-snmp, disabling SNMP notifications, restricting access, and rotating Zimbra secrets.

  • Attackers exploited CVE-2026-73570, an unauthenticated command-injection flaw in Zimbra Collaboration Suite that can enable remote code execution when SNMP notifications are enabled and zimbra-snmp is installed.
  • Zimbra patched the flaw in version 10.1.20, released in July 2026, and CISA later added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
  • Microsoft observed attackers deploying JSP web shells and reverse shells, escalating privileges, establishing persistence, and accessing email, authentication secrets, and mailbox data on compromised servers.
  • The attackers used Zimbra configuration data and LDAP queries to obtain high-value authentication attributes, and used Zimbra SSH credentials and rsync to move web shells and scripts between trusted cluster nodes.
  • Organizations are advised to apply updates immediately; if patching is not possible, they should remove zimbra-snmp, disable SNMP notifications, restrict SNMP and SMTP access, rotate Zimbra secrets, and scan for persistent web shells.

Technologies: web-server, database, remote-access, object-storage

Products: zimbra-collaboration-suite, zimbra-snmp, apache-jetty, mysql, azcopy, openssl, zimdown2, zimclient2

Vendors: zimbra, microsoft, apache-software-foundation, oracle, openssl-project

CISA warns of critical pre-auth RCE flaw in MikroTik RouterOS — Should Read

CISA warns that CVE-2026-84411 is a critical pre-authentication flaw in MikroTik RouterOS web management that can let an unauthenticated attacker execute code as root or crash affected routers with one crafted request. Organizations should update RouterOS and ensure management interfaces are not exposed to the internet.

  • CISA warned that CVE-2026-84411 is a critical pre-authentication integer-underflow flaw in MikroTik RouterOS web-management HTTP request handling.
  • A single crafted request can allow an unauthenticated network attacker to execute code with root privileges or cause a denial of service.
  • CISA said RouterOS versions below 7.24 are affected, while also noting that MikroTik recommends updating to version 7.23 or later, creating ambiguity about the affected versions.
  • CISA said it has no knowledge of active exploitation of CVE-2026-84411, but recommended keeping control systems inaccessible from the internet and using firewalls and updated VPNs for remote access.
  • The latest stable RouterOS release cited in the article is 7.24.4, and the latest long-term release is 7.23.7.

Technologies: router, operating-system

Products: routeros

Vendors: mikrotik

Attackers Abuse MSP360 to Deploy ScreenConnect in Dual-RMM Phishing Attacks — Should Read

Microsoft warned that phishing campaigns are disguising legitimate MSP360 installers as meeting invites, PDFs, and software updates to establish persistent remote access. Attackers then deploy ConnectWise ScreenConnect as a second remote-management channel to transfer tools, collect data, and steal credentials while blending into normal IT activity.

  • Microsoft detected phishing campaigns in July 2026 that distributed a digitally signed MSP360 RMM installer disguised as meeting invitations, PDF-related files, software updates, and other social-engineering lures.
  • After MSP360 is installed, the attackers use it to run PowerShell and stealthily install ConnectWise ScreenConnect, creating a second remote-access channel on affected devices.
  • The MSP360 installer establishes persistence by registering Windows services and registry autorun entries, and it modifies the Windows Firewall to allow inbound UDP traffic on port 48678 for RMM.Agent.exe.
  • The dual use of MSP360 and ScreenConnect lets attackers transfer and run additional tools, collect information, and conduct credential-access operations while blending in with ordinary remote-administration activity.
  • Microsoft also observed separate July 2026 attacks that used Faronics Deploy Agent instead of MSP360 before downloading and installing ScreenConnect.

Technologies: operating-system, remote-access, cloud-platform, object-storage, source-control

Products: windows, msp360-rmm, connectwise-screenconnect, faronics-deploy-agent, amazon-s3, cloudflare-r2, dropbox, gitlab, supabase

Vendors: microsoft, msp360, connectwise, faronics, amazon-web-services, cloudflare, dropbox, gitlab, supabase

Attackers Abuse ChatGPT Custom GPTs to Deliver RAT via ClickFix Lures — Should Read

Attackers are using malicious ChatGPT Custom GPTs promoted in Google search results to redirect users to ClickFix pages that trick them into running PowerShell and installing a feature-rich RAT. The campaign has infected at least 40 users and uses Google Sites, DLL sideloading, encrypted WAV payloads, and DNS-over-HTTPS to evade detection.

  • Threat actors created ChatGPT Custom GPTs named "Plus 5.6" that directed users to Google Sites links under the guise of a service availability notice.
  • The Google Sites pages displayed fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA checks that used ClickFix prompts to trick victims into copying and running a malicious PowerShell command.
  • The PowerShell command downloaded an MSI installer that abused Canon-signed COTFileReadApp.exe to sideload altered DLLs and ultimately launch a RAT payload.
  • Huntress reported that at least 40 users were infected in the campaign, and the RAT can collect system information, access cameras and microphones, search files, run remote desktop sessions, and execute additional payloads.
  • The RAT uses DNS-over-HTTPS through Cloudflare, Google, and Quad9 resolvers to locate its command-and-control server while blending its requests into normal HTTPS traffic.

Technologies: cloud-platform, browser, operating-system, antivirus

Products: chatgpt, custom-gpts, google-sites, google-chrome, windows, microsoft-defender, cotfilereadapp

Vendors: openai, google, cloudflare, canon, microsoft, quad9

Opsec Fail Leaks a Rare Look Inside a Media-Buy-Powered Scam Operation — Should Read

A leaked backend backup exposed a South Africa-focused investment-scam operation that used Keitaro cloaking, paid-ad attribution, fake news sites, and automated lead delivery to a CRM and Telegram. The leak reveals a likely shared scam toolkit operating across multiple domains and geographies, along with exposed infrastructure and bot credentials.

  • A leaked ZIP backup at the root of boroxior.pro exposed eight branded investment-scam pages targeting South Africa and impersonating outlets and institutions including News24, SABC News, Bloomberg, SMWX, and the South African government.
  • The scam pages used Keitaro at lonvexo.xyz to decide whether visitors received a harmless decoy page or the scam content, based on factors such as location and whether the visitor appeared to be a bot, ad reviewer, or VPN user.
  • The lead forms collected names, email addresses, phone numbers, IP addresses, and advertising campaign data, then sent records to a CRM endpoint, Keitaro, an ad attribution pixel, and a private Telegram chat.
  • The exposed send.php script contained a Telegram bot token and chat ID, and the article states that possession of the token could permit control of the bot and access to incoming lead messages.
  • A GitHub-hosted flag-sprite asset associated with the toolkit received more than 3.8 million jsDelivr requests over a year, while URLScan matches linked the shared toolkit to scam pages targeting European audiences.

Technologies: source-control

Products: keitaro, telegram-bot-api, github, jsdelivr, facebook-pixel, ipapi

Vendors: keitaro, telegram, github, jsdelivr, meta, ipapi

2CLoader: A New Malware Loader Delivering Vidar and Remus — Should Read

Zscaler researchers identified 2CLoader, a highly configurable Windows malware loader that uses extensive anti-analysis and evasion techniques to deliver Vidar, Remus, and XWorm payloads. Its capabilities include indirect system calls, VM/debugger checks, API hooks, multiple persistence options, and in-memory payload execution.

  • Zscaler ThreatLabz identified 2CLoader in August 2026 as a Windows loader used to distribute Vidar, Remus, and XWorm RAT.
  • 2CLoader uses anti-analysis and evasion features including virtual-machine and debugger checks, indirect system calls, user-activity checks, and inline hooks placed in Windows API functions.
  • The loader stores its configuration and encrypted payload in a PE resource, derives an AES-256 key from the SHA-256 hash of its first executable section, and decrypts the payload with AES-GCM.
  • 2CLoader can establish persistence through Registry Run and RunOnce entries, the Startup folder, scheduled tasks, the Windows Load value, and the UserInitMprLogonScript value.
  • 2CLoader sends XOR-encrypted JSON status messages to its command-and-control server through HTTP POST requests, beginning with a registration message containing host and configuration details.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: zscaler-cloud-sandbox, windows

Vendors: zscaler, microsoft

AI's Third Wave: Coworkers Break the Security Model That Worked for Agents — Optional

Persistent AI coworkers will need dedicated, governable identities rather than borrowed human credentials, because standing access, access creep, and inaccurate audit logs make current agent access models unsafe. The sponsored article argues organizations should discover unregistered agents, assign owners and least-privilege scopes, rotate credentials, and automatically retire inactive or orphaned agents.

  • The article describes persistent AI coworkers as a third wave of work-related AI that requires access to company data, cloud infrastructure, and other workplace systems without relying on approval for every action.
  • The article says most deployed AI agent platforms currently use OAuth grants, in-session handoffs, service accounts, or static bearer tokens instead of identities created specifically for agents.
  • When an AI system uses a human’s granted permissions, audit logs commonly record the human as the actor, making it difficult to accurately attribute actions.
  • Persistent AI coworkers can accumulate access across projects, and several individually reasonable permissions can combine into broader access that no one intended to grant.
  • The article recommends finding unregistered agents through authentication activity, assigning each persistent agent its own identity and human owner, limiting its permissions, and defining when its access expires.

Technologies: iam, identity-provider, pam

Products: entra-agent-id, universal-directory, chatgpt, chatgpt-work, codex, google-workspace

Vendors: token-security, microsoft, openai, anthropic, google, okta, sailpoint, cyberark

Why a global financial company replaced three data sources with one — Optional

Silent Push says its unified API consolidates actively resolved DNS, WHOIS, and web-scan data, allowing a global fintech to replace three separate data integrations with one for infrastructure risk analysis.

  • A security engineer at a global fintech was building an internal graph to map risk dynamically across the company’s infrastructure using external data combined with internal signals.
  • The team previously had to query separate DNS, WHOIS, and web-scan sources, each with different formats, access methods, and data gaps.
  • Silent Push provides DNS, WHOIS, and web-scan data through one API, replacing three separate integrations for the analyst’s team.
  • Silent Push says it collects domains and IP addresses from zone files and certificate transparency logs, then actively resolves the full dataset daily.
  • The platform continuously indexes registration changes, hosting patterns, SSL certificates, favicon hashes, HTML content, and more than 150 other metadata attributes.

Products: silent-push

Vendors: silent-push

Varonis and Cohesity: Improving Cyber Resilience with Data Security — Optional

Varonis and Cohesity promote an integrated approach to securing backup data by classifying sensitive information, enforcing least-privilege access, detecting suspicious activity, and enabling faster ransomware recovery. The partnership also aims to reduce backup storage costs by identifying and removing redundant or obsolete data.

  • Varonis integrates with Cohesity to identify and classify sensitive and regulated data stored across Cohesity Data Cloud.
  • Varonis maps data permissions and can automate granular access changes to reduce unnecessary exposure of backup data.
  • Varonis monitors user and non-human identity behavior for suspicious data access, lateral movement, privilege escalation, and abnormal file activity associated with ransomware.
  • Cohesity protects data with AES-256 encryption, multifactor authentication, DataLock for WORM, and FIPS-compliant encryption, and maintains fully hydrated snapshots for rapid restoration.
  • Varonis Data Lifecycle Management identifies redundant, obsolete, and trivial data so organizations can archive or dispose of it and reduce protected storage costs.

Technologies: backup, object-storage, mfa

Products: cohesity-data-cloud, varonis-managed-data-detection-and-response, varonis-data-lifecycle-management, datalock

Vendors: varonis, cohesity

item.title: Star Blizzard phishing, TeamViewer CVE-2026-92370, and Bitget’s $387.5M breach
item.content:encoded:
Window: 30 Sep 10:00 → 30 Sep 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

Bitget hacked via zero-day in third-party security products — Must Read

Bitget says attackers stole $387.5 million from its hot and warm wallets after exploiting zero-day flaws in two unnamed third-party security appliances, then moving laterally into its production wallet environment. Investigators found web shells, malware, and a custom withdrawal tool; Bitget attributes the heist to North Korean hackers.

  • Bitget said attackers stole $387.5 million from its hot and warm cryptocurrency wallets after exploiting zero-day flaws in two third-party security appliances.
  • SlowMist and Mandiant found that the attackers used compromised security appliances to gain persistent access and move laterally to Bitget’s production wallet job server.
  • Investigators reported that the attackers deployed a web shell, malicious packages, and a custom withdrawal tool to carry out transfers over nearly three hours on September 25.
  • Bitget suspended withdrawals after detecting unauthorized transfers and later launched a Recovery Bounty Program offering a 5% reward for help recovering or freezing stolen funds.
  • Bitget CEO Gracy Chen attributed the incident to North Korean hackers, citing IP behavior patterns and on-chain analysis.

Vendors: slowmist, google-cloud, mandiant

Russian FSB-linked hackers scale up phishing attacks against Ukraine supporters — Should Read

Microsoft says the FSB-linked Star Blizzard group has expanded from targeted Ukraine-focused phishing to large-scale campaigns against more than 100 organizations, mainly in the U.S. and UK. The group now uses the RedFlick delivery method to install the CosmicPulse backdoor with fewer victim actions and improved evasion.

  • Microsoft reported that the Russian FSB-linked Star Blizzard group has expanded phishing operations in 2026, affecting more than 100 organizations primarily in the United States and United Kingdom.
  • Star Blizzard has targeted Ukrainian individuals and institutions as well as NGOs, think tanks, governments, and financial institutions that support Ukraine politically or financially.
  • Microsoft identified at least 13 large-scale phishing campaigns since January, reflecting a shift from highly targeted messages to campaigns involving tens or hundreds of emails.
  • Since March, the group has used accounts created on compromised websites and often sent fake conference or event invitations impersonating reputable think tanks or NGOs.
  • Star Blizzard’s RedFlick technique uses a password-protected archive and scheduled tasks to install the CosmicPulse backdoor after a victim opens a file, requiring only one victim action.

Technologies: email-security

Products: cosmicpulse, redflick, clickfix

Vendors: microsoft, ukr-net

TeamViewer urges users to patch severe flaws “as soon as possible” — Should Read

TeamViewer urges customers to update Full Client and Host software to version 15.82 immediately to fix five high-severity flaws, including an access-control bypass that could enable unauthorized remote code execution. The company says it has seen no evidence of public exploits or active exploitation.

  • TeamViewer urged customers to update TeamViewer Full Client and Host software to version 15.82 as soon as possible to address five high-severity vulnerabilities.
  • The most severe issue, CVE-2026-92370, is an access-control weakness in TeamViewer software for Windows, Linux, and macOS that could allow unauthorized remote actions leading to code execution on affected systems.
  • The other four flaws include a path traversal issue, a heap-based buffer overflow, a race condition, and improper path validation that could enable local attackers to execute code or elevate privileges.
  • TeamViewer stated that the vulnerabilities are fixed in version 15.82 and supported maintenance and legacy releases, and that it is unaware of public disclosure or active exploitation.
  • The article notes that criminals, including ransomware groups, have previously abused TeamViewer remote-access software to access victims' systems and deploy malicious tools.

Technologies: remote-access

Products: teamviewer-full-client, teamviewer-host

Vendors: teamviewer

AI Coding Agents Exposed 13,000 Internal Images, Including Billing Records, on GitHub — Should Read

AI coding agents and the gitshot tool exposed more than 13,000 internal screenshots—including billing records and unreleased product details—by uploading them to public GitHub repositories under developers’ personal accounts. Organizations should audit personal GitHub repositories, releases, and gists, remove exposed files, rotate visible credentials, and restrict agents from creating public repositories.

  • Glow reported finding more than 13,000 internal images from developers at over 300 organizations in public GitHub repositories, including customer billing records and unreleased product screens.
  • The images were commonly uploaded to public repositories under developers’ personal GitHub accounts after coding agents were asked to provide screenshots of changes for code review.
  • Glow said that storing screenshots in a private repository could result in broken images for reviewers, leading agents to host the files separately in public repositories.
  • About one-third of the affected organizations had developers using gitshot, which by default uploads screenshots as publicly accessible release assets in a personal GitHub repository named gitshot-images.
  • GitHub CLI version 2.99.0, released September 1, added an --attach option for attaching images to pull requests, issues, and comments with repository write access.

Technologies: source-control

Products: github, github-cli, claude-code, gitshot

Vendors: glow, github, anthropic, gitshot

Microsoft to block Entra ID script injection attacks starting October — Should Read

Microsoft will enforce a Content Security Policy for browser-based Entra ID sign-ins beginning in mid-October 2026, allowing only trusted Microsoft-hosted scripts and blocking externally injected code. Organizations should identify and replace browser extensions or tools that inject scripts into login pages before the rollout completes.

  • Microsoft will begin enforcing additional Content Security Policy protections for browser-based Entra ID sign-ins in mid-October 2026, with rollout expected to finish by late October 2026.
  • The policy will allow scripts only from trusted Microsoft content delivery network domains and block external or injected code on Entra ID sign-in pages.
  • Microsoft advises organizations to stop using browser extensions and tools that inject code into sign-in pages and to test sign-in scenarios before the change takes effect.
  • Users will still be able to sign in if unsupported script-injection tools cease functioning, and the update requires no tenant configuration.
  • Microsoft Authentication Library and API-based authentication flows are not affected because the enforcement applies only to browser sign-ins through login.microsoftonline.com.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam, mfa, email-security, operating-system

Products: microsoft-entra-id, microsoft-authentication-library, microsoft-365, office-2024, exchange-online, windows

Vendors: microsoft

An ISP DKIM-Signed This Brand Impersonation — May Read

A phishing email impersonating a UK pharmacy chain passed SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and composite authentication because it was legitimately sent and signed through a consumer ISP’s mail platform. The incident shows that email authentication verifies domain authorization, not the true author or legitimacy of a brand-themed message.

  • A UK fresh-produce wholesaler received a survey phishing email on 14 February 2026 that impersonated a major UK pharmacy chain and linked to a replica storefront page.
  • The email passed SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and composite authentication because it was sent through and signed by a consumer ISP using the ISP’s own domain.
  • The sender used a pharmacy-brand display name with a rewards-themed mailbox on an unrelated consumer ISP domain, while the landing page showed outdated Christmas promotions.
  • The recipient’s mail system recorded SCL:-1 and SFV:SKN, indicating the message was marked non-spam before filtering ran due to a recipient-side allow-list entry or mail flow rule.
  • The article emphasizes that email authentication verifies authorization to use a domain but does not establish who authored a message or whether a claimed brand relationship is genuine.

Technologies: email-security, object-storage, cloud-platform

Products: ironscales-adaptive-ai, amazon-s3

Vendors: ironscales, amazon

US-Focused CSuite Phishing Steals Microsoft 365 Sessions and Deploys RMM Tools for Remote Access — May Read

A US-focused CSuite phishing campaign uses business-themed lures to steal Microsoft 365 sessions and deploy legitimate RMM tools such as ScreenConnect and Action1, giving attackers both account and endpoint access. The activity is concentrated in the United States and targets business-critical sectors including technology, manufacturing, government, and consulting.

  • ANY.RUN traced the US-focused CSuite phishing campaign across 351 sandbox analyses, with 51% of related submissions originating in the United States.
  • CSuite uses lures impersonating services including Adobe, DocuSign, Zoom, Google Meet, Dropbox, and Microsoft 365.
  • The campaign can install legitimate remote-management tools such as ScreenConnect or Action1 through installers, archives, or BAT/VBS droppers, providing attackers remote access to endpoints.
  • CSuite also uses credential-harvesting and device-code phishing flows intended to capture Microsoft 365 access and active sessions.
  • Technology, manufacturing, government and administration, and consulting were among the sectors most exposed to CSuite activity in the analyzed corpus.

Technologies: cloud-platform, identity-provider, remote-access

Products: interactive-sandbox, threat-intelligence-lookup, threat-intelligence-feeds, microsoft-365, screenconnect, action1

Vendors: any-run, microsoft, connectwise, action1

Know Your Enemy: Browser-Based Attack Techniques in 2026 — Optional

Browser-based threats are increasingly driving the full breach lifecycle, using techniques such as AiTM phishing, ClickFix, OAuth authorization phishing, malicious extensions, credential stuffing, and stolen-session replay to bypass traditional email, endpoint, and MFA defenses. Security teams need visibility and controls within browser sessions, including extension governance, identity hardening, and detection of suspicious user interactions.

  • Modern reverse-proxy phishing kits such as Tycoon2FA, Sneaky2FA, and Evilginx can intercept credentials and live session tokens in real time, bypassing most forms of multi-factor authentication.
  • ClickFix attacks use fake CAPTCHA or verification prompts to persuade users to copy and execute malicious commands, and Push reported that ClickFix accounted for 52% of its detections in Q2 2026.
  • Authorization phishing abuses OAuth consent grants, device code flows, and token exchanges to obtain access tokens without stealing credentials during the sign-in process.
  • Push found that 46.76% of browser extensions used by its customers had permission combinations capable of enabling account takeover without user interaction.
  • Stolen session tokens, often obtained through infostealer malware, can be replayed in an attacker-controlled browser to bypass authentication, including passkeys.

  • The attackers deployed WHIPSHOT, a PHP web shell that receives Base64-encoded commands through HTTP headers, and SLAPSHOT, a Python tool that forwards network traffic to internal hosts.
  • The attackers modified NetScaler web-server configuration files to execute files disguised as Debian packages or signature files as PHP scripts and, in some cases, to make image-request URLs trigger hidden web shells.
  • GreyNoise reported that activity involving CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 escalated from mass reconnaissance to broad exploitation and web-shell and malware deployment on September 28, 2026.

OpenSSL Fixes High-Severity DTLS Flaw That Can Leak Heap Memory Unencrypted — Should Read

OpenSSL has patched CVE-2026-84782, a high-severity DTLS flaw that can expose unencrypted heap memory to a peer or crash affected applications. Organizations using OpenSSL for DTLS should upgrade to 4.0.3, 3.6.5, 3.5.9, or 3.4.8, or apply their distribution’s patched package.

  • OpenSSL fixed CVE-2026-84782, a high-severity DTLS flaw that can leak heap memory as unencrypted handshake data to a connection peer or crash an affected program.
  • The issue occurs when a DTLS handshake message is only partly sent and the resend timer retransmits an earlier message using the wrong position in the buffer.
  • Public fixes are available in OpenSSL 4.0.3, 3.6.5, 3.5.9, and 3.4.8, while fixes for the older 3.0, 1.1.1, and 1.0.2 branches are available only to premium support customers.

  • Ubuntu and Debian released patched OpenSSL packages, while OpenSSL listed no workaround for users who cannot update.

Microsoft Breach by Midnight Blizzard (APT29): What Happened? — Should Read

Midnight Blizzard (APT29) reportedly used password spraying against a poorly secured Microsoft test tenant, then abused legacy OAuth app permissions and Entra ID roles to create persistent malicious applications with broad Exchange Online mailbox access. The incident highlights the need for MFA everywhere, strict least-privilege controls, and continuous auditing of app registrations, service principals, and consent grants.

  • The article attributes the Microsoft campaign to Midnight Blizzard, also known as APT29 or Cozy Bear, and describes the group as linked to Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR).
  • The attackers obtained initial access by password spraying a non-production Microsoft test tenant that lacked multi-factor authentication.
  • The article says the attackers abused a legacy OAuth application and Microsoft Entra ID permissions to create a new user and assign high-privilege roles in Microsoft’s corporate tenant.
  • The attackers created malicious OAuth applications and granted them the Office 365 Exchange Online full_access_as_app permission, enabling access to corporate mailboxes.
  • The article recommends enforcing multi-factor authentication, auditing permissions and application registrations, monitoring unusual activity, and securing legacy and test systems.

How Okta Passwords Can Be Compromised: Uncovering a Risk to User Data — Should Read

Okta audit logs can store passwords in plaintext when users mistakenly enter them in the username field during a failed login, exposing credentials to anyone with access to those logs or forwarded SIEM data. Organizations should identify and rotate affected credentials, restrict log access, and enforce phishing-resistant MFA.

  • Okta audit logs can record a password in plaintext when a user mistakenly enters it in the username field during a failed login attempt.
  • People who can read Okta audit logs, including through a SIEM system where those logs are forwarded, may be able to access exposed user passwords.
  • Mitiga reported identifying hundreds of potentially leaked passwords and credentials for customers, including administrator-level users, by matching failed and successful login events.
  • Multi-factor authentication can reduce the risk from exposed passwords, but the article notes that phishing, repeated approval requests, and session hijacking may still be used to bypass it.

New Spectre-v2 BTR Attack Leaks Linux Memory Despite Existing Defenses — Should Read

Researchers disclosed Branch Target Reuse (BTR), a new Spectre-v2 technique that abuses stale branch-prediction entries in JIT engines to transiently execute reused code locations and leak secrets. Proof-of-concept Linux kernel exploits recovered a root password hash from fully patched Intel systems, and fixes have been merged for the affected cBPF JIT.

  • Researchers from VUSec and Scuola Superiore Sant'Anna disclosed Branch Target Reuse (BTR), a new Spectre-v2 variant affecting JIT engines.
  • BTR exploits stale indirect branch-prediction entries that can remain after JIT-generated code is freed and its memory is reused, enabling transient control-flow hijacking and data disclosure.
  • The researchers found SpiderMonkey, GraalVM, and the Linux kernel's cBPF JIT affected, with differing exploitability and data-leakage rates.
  • Two proof-of-concept Linux kernel exploits recovered a root password hash within minutes from a fully patched Intel system with default protections enabled.
  • Linux mitigations for BTR were released and merged as CVE-2026-64507 and CVE-2026-64508, while GraalVM randomized JIT code-cache locations and Mozilla is prioritizing site isolation.

item.content:encoded:
Window: 29 Sep 10:00 → 29 Sep 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

Here We Go Again (Citrix NetScaler DTLS Preauth Memory Overflow CVE-2026-88772) — Must Read

CVE-2026-88772 is an actively exploited, pre-authentication DTLS memory overflow in Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway VPN virtual servers with DTLS enabled by default, which can lead to remote code execution. Organizations should urgently upgrade to Citrix's fixed releases or disable DTLS where operationally feasible.

  • CVE-2026-88772 is a Citrix NetScaler DTLS memory overflow that can cause remote code execution or denial of service before authentication when DTLS is enabled.
  • Citrix reported CVE-2026-88772 as exploited in the wild, and DTLS is enabled by default on NetScaler VPN virtual servers unless an administrator turns it off.
  • The vulnerable NetScaler 14.1-73.30 code copies a reassembled chain of packet buffers into a fixed 35,840-byte scratch buffer without checking the total size.
  • The article demonstrates that 120 crafted DTLS records can cause approximately 173,665 bytes to be copied, overflowing the scratch buffer by 137,825 bytes.
  • Citrix recommends upgrading NetScaler ADC and Gateway to fixed releases including 14.1-73.37 or later and 13.1-64.23 or later.

Technologies: load-balancer, vpn, remote-access

Products: citrix-netscaler-adc, citrix-netscaler-gateway

Vendors: citrix, cloud-software-group

Building a certificate authority for the whole Internet — Should Read

Cloudflare plans to become a publicly trusted certificate authority, combining a newly applied-for root program presence with an acquired GlobalSign root to provide broadly compatible, automated TLS certificates. It also intends to support ACME-first issuance and post-quantum Merkle Tree Certificates beginning in early 2027.

  • Cloudflare announced its intent to become a publicly trusted certificate authority but stated that it is not issuing certificates yet.
  • Cloudflare has applied to the Chrome, Apple, Microsoft, and Mozilla root programs and signed a definitive agreement to acquire an established broadly trusted root from GlobalSign.
  • Cloudflare plans to offer automated certificate issuance and renewal through ACME, requiring customers to support ACME Renewal Information for issuance.
  • Cloudflare intends to publish reproducible builds of its certificate-signing software, attest the hardware security modules holding its keys, and operate a public dashboard for issuance health and incidents.
  • Cloudflare plans to issue production post-quantum Merkle Tree Certificates in the first quarter of 2027.

Russian pizza chain with 1,500 locations confirms cyberattack following hacker claims — Should Read

Dodo Pizza confirmed that hackers accessed customer personal and order data after DataSuckers claimed it stole records for 68 million customers, though the scope remains unverified. The company says payment data was not affected, attacker access has been blocked, and an investigation is underway.

The Arizona Supreme Court says criminal hackers copied personally identifiable information belonging to many Arizona residents from the state court system. The incident was not ransomware and no ransom demand has been reported; officials are notifying affected people and working with the FBI.

A Vietnamese national, Trung Nguyen Van, was charged in the U.S. with laundering cryptocurrency tied to pig-butchering scams, including about $16 million stolen from one victim. Authorities say his wallets received more than $53 million from fraud schemes targeting U.S. victims between 2018 and 2024.

It Failed Three Auth Checks, Then Got Whitelisted — Should Read

A phishing email spoofing the victim’s own domain failed reverse-DNS, SPF, and DMARC checks at a hosted relay but was still whitelisted, then re-injected through the organization’s Exchange infrastructure and delivered by Microsoft 365 as internal mail. The case shows how sender-based allowlisting and downstream authentication of relays rather than original senders can launder forged phishing messages.

  • A phishing message spoofing the recipient organization’s own domain arrived from external IP address 38.46.218.158 and failed reverse-DNS, SPF, and DMARC checks at a hosted filtering relay.
  • Despite those failures, the relay classified the message as whitelisted with sender-based evidence and recommended that it be accepted.
  • The message was re-injected through the organization’s on-premises Exchange 2019 server and outbound host, then reached Microsoft 365 with SPF, DMARC, and composite authentication marked as passed and was classified as internal mail.
  • Four mailboxes at a privately held UK industrial firm received the message within six minutes, and the lure used a DocuSign-style completed-document theme with a link through emj.to.
  • The sender history for the forged domain showed 39 incidents since March 2025, with 37 automatically resolved as malicious, one human malicious verdict, and no safe verdicts.

Technologies: email-security

Products: microsoft-365, exchange-server-2019, spamexperts, exim

Vendors: microsoft, spamexperts, ironscales, exim-project, docusign

OperTraitors: How Kubernetes Operators Betray Your Security Posture — May Read

Kubernetes operators frequently receive excessive RBAC privileges, making a compromised operator a potential cluster-wide backdoor; Unit 42’s OperTraitor tool found issues including IBM Turbonomic Prometurbo’s former cluster-wide secret access (CVE-2026-6389). Organizations should verify operator provenance, minimize and continuously audit service-account permissions, and closely monitor operator behavior—especially as AI-driven operators expand the potential impact.

  • Kubernetes operators rely on service accounts with role-based access control permissions, so the impact of an operator compromise is defined by the permissions granted to that account.
  • Unit 42 released OperTraitor, an open-source LLM-powered tool that compares an operator’s documented functionality with its actual permissions and assigns a risk score from 1 to 10.
  • OperTraitor identified cluster-wide secret-reading permissions in IBM Turbonomic’s Prometurbo operator, leading to CVE-2026-6389 with a CVSS score of 8.8 after IBM issued a fix.
  • The article warns that outdated and abandoned operators in OperatorHub can retain excessive permissions, and recommends verifying sources, limiting operators to necessary namespaces, auditing permissions, and monitoring service-account activity.

Technologies: container-platform, orchestration, iam

Products: opertraitor, kubernetes, ibm-turbonomic-application-resource-management, prometurbo, datadog-operator, operatorhub, operator-lifecycle-manager, cortex-cloud

Vendors: palo-alto-networks, ibm, datadog, red-hat

Cloudflare has added per-domain visibility into TLS key-exchange groups across HTTP Traffic Analytics, Logpush, and Log Explorer, allowing customers to measure adoption of post-quantum X25519MLKEM768 encryption for visitor and origin connections. The telemetry helps organizations identify classical-cryptography gaps and prepare for post-quantum migration deadlines.

  • Customers can use the ClientTLSKeyExchangeGroup log field to determine whether individual visitor connections use post-quantum X25519MLKEM768 or classical key-exchange methods.
  • Cloudflare also added the OriginTLSKeyExchangeGroup Logpush field to show the key-exchange group used between Cloudflare and an origin server.
  • Cloudflare Radar reports that about 70% of browser-generated traffic reaching Cloudflare uses hybrid ML-KEM, while about 15% of origins connected by Cloudflare use hybrid ML-KEM.
  • Cloudflare states that customers with legacy origin servers can use Cloudflare Tunnel to carry traffic to Cloudflare over TLS 1.3 with X25519MLKEM768 without upgrading the legacy server.

Enforce positive security with Cloudflare Application Profiles — Optional

Cloudflare has launched Application Profiles, which learn normal HTTP request structures and flag deviations so customers can enforce positive security policies for web applications and APIs. The feature is available to API Security customers and in closed beta for invited Enterprise customers.

  • Cloudflare launched Application Profiles to learn the expected structure and format of HTTP requests and identify requests that do not conform to those learned profiles.
  • Schema Profiles can learn path variables, query parameters, headers, cookies, and JSON or form-encoded request bodies, including data types and constraints such as numeric ranges and string character classes.
  • The validation signal does not block requests automatically; customers can review results in Security Analytics and create Security Rules to monitor or block non-conforming requests.
  • An operation requires at least 1,000 requests with 2xx responses in the preceding seven days to learn fields and at least 10,000 requests to learn data boundaries.

Apple patches CoreGraphics zero-day flaw exploited in attacks — Must Read

Apple patched an actively exploited CoreGraphics out-of-bounds write zero-day that can enable arbitrary code execution through a maliciously crafted file. Users should promptly update affected iPhones, iPads, and Macs to iOS/iPadOS 26.7.1 or macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 and Sequoia 15.8.1.

  • Apple released security updates for a CoreGraphics out-of-bounds write flaw that it says may have been exploited in extremely sophisticated, targeted attacks against individuals using iOS versions before iOS 27.
  • Processing a maliciously crafted file could allow arbitrary code execution, and Apple addressed the issue with improved bounds checking.
  • Apple patched the issue in iOS and iPadOS 26.7.1, macOS Tahoe 26.7.1, and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1.
  • The affected devices include iPhone 11 and later, several iPad models, and Macs running macOS Sequoia 15.8.1 or Tahoe 26.7.1.
  • The article advises users to install the security updates promptly, despite the reported exploitation being limited to highly targeted attacks.

Technologies: operating-system, mobile-os

Products: coregraphics, ios, ipados, macos, macos-tahoe, macos-sequoia, iphone, ipad

Vendors: apple, meta

Dutch Police Arrest 24-Year-Old Amsterdam Man in ShinyHunters Investigation — Should Read

Dutch police arrested a 24-year-old Amsterdam man reportedly linked to ShinyHunters, while the group remains under scrutiny following its claimed breach of the FBI’s job application site. The group says the intrusion exploited Oracle PeopleSoft protections via URL-encoding to bypass WAF rules.

  • Dutch authorities arrested a 24-year-old Amsterdam man in connection with an investigation into the ShinyHunters hacking group.
  • Police said the arrested individual is expected to appear before the Rotterdam District Court on September 29, 2026.
  • Brian Krebs and DataBreaches.Net identified the arrested man as Pepijn van der Stap, also known as Umbreon, who was previously apprehended in 2023 in connection with data thefts and extortion.
  • ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for accessing the FBI job application website and stealing terabytes of sensitive data.
  • The group said it used a URL-encoding method to bypass web application firewall rules related to CVE-2026-35273 in Oracle PeopleSoft.

Technologies: waf

Products: oracle-peoplesoft

Vendors: oracle

Official MCP Python SDK Flaw Can Let Malicious Servers Steal OAuth Credentials — Should Read

A high-severity flaw in the official MCP Python SDK could let malicious MCP servers redirect OAuth exchanges and steal client secrets, authorization codes, and PKCE verifiers. Users should upgrade to versions 1.30.0 or 2.2.0, configure an explicit issuer for machine-to-machine OAuth providers, and rotate credentials if untrusted servers may have been used.

  • A flaw in affected versions of the official MCP Python SDK could allow a malicious MCP server to redirect OAuth token exchanges and receive a client secret, authorization code, and PKCE proof key.
  • The issue affects HTTP MCP clients using OAuthClientProvider, ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider, PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider, or the deprecated RFC7523OAuthClientProvider when they can connect to servers they do not fully control.
  • Cycode demonstrated that stolen credentials could be used to obtain a valid access token from the real login service with the permissions granted to the application.
  • The issue is fixed in MCP Python SDK version 1.30.0 for the 1.x line and version 2.2.0 for the 2.x line.
  • Users of ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider or PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider must also supply an explicit issuer setting, while users who may have contacted untrusted servers should rotate client secrets and revoke tokens.

Technologies: iam

Products: mcp-python-sdk

Kiteworks restored hosted customer systems and lifted its shutdown advisory after patching a critical flaw in Advanced Forms, saying it found no evidence of compromise or exploitation.

item.title: Hugging Face Details Five-Day Agentic Kubernetes-to-Cloud Intrusion
item.content:encoded:
Window: 29 Sep 02:00 → 29 Sep 06:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hugging Face Agentic Attack: We Ran It Against Ourselves — May Read

Mitiga used Hugging Face’s disclosed autonomous-agent intrusion as a model to assess whether its platform could detect and respond to a multi-stage attack spanning Kubernetes, AWS, identity, and source control. It argues that stopping such attacks depends on near-real-time telemetry, workload-identity detections, rapid cross-platform correlation and triage, and pre-approved response actions.

  • Hugging Face reported that an autonomous agent operated inside its production infrastructure for about five days and that the decisive escalation from in-cluster reconnaissance to cluster administrator access took about thirteen hours.
  • The modeled intrusion moved across Kubernetes, AWS, an internal network, and source control by using service-account and cloud credentials, with evidence distributed across separate log sources.
  • Mitiga says that stopping this type of intrusion requires timely data collection, detections that apply to workload identities, correlation and triage of related signals within a relevant time window, and response action.
  • The article distinguishes correlation, which assembles events into incident candidates, from triage, which judges a candidate’s severity and whether it should wake an on-call responder.
  • The article argues that organizations should decide and approve autonomous containment actions before an incident, balancing the action’s consequence and reversibility.

Technologies: container-platform, orchestration, cloud-platform, source-control, iam, soar

Products: panoramic-awareness, ai-triage, helios-aidr, kubernetes, aws

Vendors: mitiga, hugging-face, amazon-web-services, kubernetes
